Ltd. 0 careers@mozilor.com Company Profile Legal Content Specialist (LLB) This role sits between our legal reality and our readers. CookieYes publishes a large library of privacy content that businesses across the world rely on to understand what the law asks of them, and we need someone professionally qualified to stand behind it. We are looking for a law graduate who writes because they want to, not because a brief demanded it. You will track privacy legislation across jurisdictions, translate it into content our customers can act on, and act as the internal check on the legal accuracy of everything we publish and ship. Part of the role is genuine legal work: reviewing our own agreements, supporting compliance queries from customers, and keeping our product claims defensible. RESPONSIBILITIES Monitor privacy and data protection developments globally, including GDPR, ePrivacy, CCPA and other US state laws, LGPD, PIPEDA, PDPA and emerging regulations, and flag what matters for CookieYes and our customers. Write authoritative long-form content: regulation explainers, jurisdiction guides, compliance checklists, legal update posts and whitepapers. Act as the legal accuracy reviewer for marketing and product content, with an agreed turnaround SLA so reviews never stall the pipeline. Nothing that makes a compliance claim should ship without your reading. Structure that content to be found and cited by AI search, AI Overviews and answer engines, working with the SEO and AI search team on generative engine optimisation, schema and citation-worthy formatting. Translate regulatory obligations into product requirements, working with product and engineering on how consent, records and disclosures need to behave. Support customer-facing compliance queries escalated by sales and support, and build the internal reference material that reduces how often they need escalating. Review and maintain our own legal documents, including the privacy policy, terms of service, DPAs and vendor agreements, with external counsel where required. Prepare briefing notes for leadership when a regulatory change affects roadmap or positioning. Represent CookieYes’s point of view publicly through bylined articles, webinars and industry commentary. REQUIREMENTS LLB or equivalent law degree from a recognised institution. Enrolment with a bar council is welcome but not required. 2+ years of relevant experience in a law firm, in-house legal team, compliance function or legal publishing role. Demonstrable writing ability outside pleadings and contracts. Send us published work, a blog, a newsletter or a substantial piece written for a non-lawyer audience. The instinct to write for a business owner rather than a bench. Accuracy without legalese. Working familiarity with data protection law, or clear evidence you can master a regulatory area quickly and thoroughly. Fluency with AI tools for research, drafting and summarisation, paired with the discipline to verify every citation, holding and date against the primary source before it reaches a draft. Research discipline: you cite primary sources, you check whether guidance has been superseded, and you do not build an argument on a secondary summary. Sound judgement about the line between explaining the law and giving legal advice, and the care to keep our content on the right side of it. GOOD TO HAVE A privacy certification such as CIPP/E, CIPP/US or CIPM, or the intent to pursue one, which we will support. Prior experience at a SaaS, privacy tech or legal tech company. Experience drafting or negotiating DPAs and SaaS agreements. Comfort with SEO, GEO and how legal content performs in traditional search, AI search and AI Overviews. Additional language ability relevant to EU jurisdictions. Good understanding of, or familiarity with, major global privacy and data protection laws, including GDPR, CCPA, DPA, PDPA, UCPA, and related regulations. Ltd. 0 careers@mozilor.com Company Profile AI Search & Agentic Growth Specialist (LLM SEO) A growing share of the people who need a consent management platform now ask an AI assistant instead of a search engine. They ask ChatGPT how to comply with GDPR, they ask Claude to add a cookie banner to the site it just built, and they read an AI Overview instead of clicking a result. CookieYes intends to be the answer in those places. This role has two halves. The first is AI search visibility: getting CookieYes recommended, cited and integrated across LLM surfaces. The second is agentic automation: building the AI workflows that let a small growth team operate like a much larger one. We are looking for someone who is genuinely hands-on with both. RESPONSIBILITIES Own CookieYes’s visibility in AI search: ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Copilot and Google AI Overviews. Define how we measure it, then improve it. Build the measurement layer for LLM visibility: prompt sets, share-of-voice tracking, citation monitoring and competitor benchmarking, so this stops being anecdotal. Run generative engine optimisation in practice: content structure, entity and schema markup, extractable formatting, and the freshness signals that make a page quotable. Identify which third-party sources LLMs cite in our category, and work with content, PR and partnerships to earn placement in them. Work with product and partnerships on distribution inside AI ecosystems, including MCP servers, connector directories and plugin marketplaces, and on integrations with AI website builders. Build agentic workflows for the growth team: competitor and regulation monitoring, content research and briefing pipelines, review and approval flows, reporting automation, and internal tooling that removes manual work. Evaluate and integrate AI tooling across the growth stack, and set the guardrails: what gets automated, what stays human-reviewed, and how we check output quality. Keep the traditional SEO fundamentals intact. AI search sits on top of technical health, internal linking and topical authority, not instead of them. Report on AI-sourced traffic, assisted signups and share of voice, and tell the team plainly what is working and what is noise. REQUIREMENTS 3+ years in SEO, content strategy or growth engineering, with demonstrable recent work on AI search, GEO, AEO or LLM visibility. Hands-on experience building agentic workflows or automations with tools such as n8n, Zapier, Make, LangChain, or direct API and MCP integrations. Working knowledge of prompt engineering and LLM behaviour, including retrieval, grounding, citation patterns and why models hallucinate a competitor’s name. Solid technical SEO foundation: crawling, indexing, structured data, site architecture and Core Web Vitals. Comfort writing scripts. Python or JavaScript at the level needed to pull APIs, parse results and build a monitoring job. The instinct to build measurement before making claims. This field is full of confident assertions with no data behind them. Clear written communication, and the honesty to say when an AI channel is not yet worth the investment. GOOD TO HAVE Experience with MCP servers, AI connector directories or plugin marketplace listings. Familiarity with tools such as Ahrefs Brand Radar, Profound, Peec AI or similar AI visibility platforms. Background in B2B SaaS, developer tooling or a technical product category. Experience with digital PR or link earning as a route to citation. Understanding of privacy and compliance as a subject area. Ltd. 0 careers@mozilor.com Company Profile Growth Lead CookieYes is a consent management platform used by over a million websites to stay compliant with GDPR, CCPA and a growing list of global privacy regulations. We are a product of Mozilor, and we sell to business owners, agencies and developers in more than 100 countries through a product-led motion and a fast-expanding marketplace and partner network. We are hiring a Growth Lead to own the full customer lifecycle: acquisition, onboarding, engagement and retention. You will write the growth plan, own the budget behind it, and be accountable for the number it produces. This is not a coordination role. You get real spend, a team to build, and the authority to decide what we try next, and in exchange we expect a high rate of shipped experiments and a straight answer every week on what worked. We are looking for someone who has done this at scale before, in a SaaS business past $10M ARR, and who runs the ship without being asked twice. RESPONSIBILITIES Own the growth plan and its implementation. Set quarterly targets across acquisition, onboarding, engagement and retention, sequence the work, and be accountable for shipping it rather than presenting it. Own the numbers end to end: signups, activation rate, free-to-paid conversion, cohort retention, churn, expansion revenue and CAC payback. Acquisition: lead across organic, paid, product-led, AI search and marketplace channels, and decide where budget and effort go each quarter. Onboarding: own the path from install to a live consent banner. Work with product to cut steps, reduce drop-off, and get every new user to first value fast. Engagement: build the lifecycle programme across email, in-app messaging and in-product prompts that brings users back into the product and deepens usage. Retention and churn: track cohort retention, diagnose where and why accounts leave, run win-back and reactivation, and take the structural fixes to product and support. Expansion: drive upgrades and plan movement through usage-based triggers, and design and analyse pricing and packaging tests with product and finance. Build and run the experimentation roadmap across the website, onboarding, pricing page, in-app upgrade paths and lifecycle email. Build the growth reporting layer. Define the metrics that matter, instrument them properly, and make the numbers legible to the wider team. Partner with the Global Partnerships and Affiliate teams so that channel growth and self-serve growth reinforce each other rather than compete. Manage and mentor a small team of specialists across performance, lifecycle, SEO and AI search, and hire into gaps as the team scales. Own the paid budget: allocate it across channels, defend the allocation with data, and reallocate the moment the data changes. Run a weekly growth review: what was shipped, what moved, what we are killing. OWNERSHIP AND WAYS OF WORKING You will own the number. Not contribute to it, not support it. If growth is behind, it is your call what changes and your job to say so early. Experiment velocity is a standing expectation, not a stretch goal. We would rather run ten tests and lose six than deliberate for a quarter and ship two. You will not be handed a backlog. You are expected to find the constraint yourself, decide what to do about it, and start. Decisions get made with the data available, not the data you wish you had. Speed of iteration beats precision of planning here. You will have real budget and the authority to move it. That comes with the obligation to report honestly when it is not working. Small team, no layers, direct access to leadership and product. Nothing about this role requires waiting for permission. REQUIREMENTS 4+ years in growth, performance or product marketing, including direct growth ownership at a B2B SaaS business at $10M+ ARR scale. Evidence you have moved a company-level number at that scale. Tell us what it was when you took it, what you changed, and where it ended up. Full-lifecycle ownership, not acquisition alone. We want to hear about a retention, onboarding or expansion number you moved, not only a channel you scaled. Experience owning a substantial paid acquisition budget, including the decision to cut spend that was not paying back. A track record of running experiments at volume, with a system for prioritising them and the discipline to kill losers quickly. Experience turning a growth plan into a sequenced roadmap and delivering against it quarter after quarter. Strong command of funnel and cohort analytics. You are comfortable in GA4, Mixpanel or Amplitude, and you pull your own data rather than waiting on someone else. Hands-on paid acquisition across Google Ads, Meta and LinkedIn, and the judgement to know when to switch a channel off. Working knowledge of SEO and content-led acquisition, enough to direct specialists and judge quality. Experience building lifecycle and in-product messaging programmes in tools such as HubSpot, Customer.io, Intercom or similar. Statistical literacy. You know what a valid test looks like and you do not call results early. Experience hiring, managing and holding a small team to account. Self-direction. You have operated without close supervision before and preferred it. GOOD TO HAVE Experience with a freemium or open-source distribution model, particularly WordPress or another CMS plugin ecosystem. Exposure to privacy, compliance, security or developer tooling markets. Experience in a product-led business that also runs partner and marketplace channels. Familiarity with how AI assistants, AI Overviews and LLM surfaces are changing discovery and search. The role involves coordinating with Loan Officers (LOs), Loan Processors (LPs), Secondary Marketing, underwriting, and investors to ensure accurate pricing, timely lock execution, and compliance with established procedures. Key Responsibilities 1. Mortgage Rate Lock Management: Process rate lock requests from Loan Officers (LOs) and Loan Processors (LPs), verify loan details (amount, program, interest rate, LTV, FICO, occupancy, property type, and lock period), ensure eligibility and compliance with company policies and investor guidelines, and accurately process new locks, changes, extensions, relocks, and cancellations on time. Monitor lock expirations, communicate confirmations, rejections, and required corrections, and maintain accurate records in the loan origination system. 2. Mortgage Pricing and Rate Sheet Management: Download and review daily investor rate sheets for dates, pricing adjustments, product availability, and lock periods. Upload and maintain rate sheets and pricing data in the pricing engine. Compare investor pricing with internal systems to identify differences. Review base pricing, loan-level price adjustments (LLPAs), margins, concessions, discount points, and lender credits. Calculate and verify final borrower or broker pricing according to company policies. Provide accurate pricing information to Loan Officers for eligible loan scenarios. 3. Lock Extensions, Relocks, and Pricing Exceptions: Review and process lock extensions, relocks, and pricing exceptions according to company policies. Calculate extension fees, relock fees, and pricing adjustments. Check lock history, expiration dates, previous extensions, and available free extension days. Process pricing concessions and exceptions only after obtaining the required approvals. Verify approval authority and maintain supporting documents. Communicate applicable fees, pricing impacts, and processing restrictions to the requesting teams. 4. Investor Guidelines and Product Eligibility: Review investor guidelines and product eligibility before processing lock requests. Verify delegated and non-delegated lending channels, where applicable. Confirm product availability based on loan program, credit score, occupancy, LTV, loan purpose, and other applicable criteria. Identify investor-specific restrictions and escalate exceptions when needed. Coordinate with investor representatives to resolve pricing, eligibility, and lock-related issues. Ensure all pricing and lock activities follow investor requirements and internal policies. 5. Communication and Issue Resolution: Respond to inquiries from Loan Officers, Loan Processors, Secondary Marketing, and other internal teams. Explain pricing differences, lock rejections, extension fees, and investor restrictions clearly. Follow up on pending lock requests, pricing exceptions, and unresolved system issues. Escalate complex pricing and eligibility concerns to the appropriate manager or authorized approver. Maintain professional communication and meet established service-level agreements (SLAs). 6. Quality Control and Reporting: Maintain accurate records of lock requests, confirmations, extensions, relocks, cancellations, and pricing exceptions. Check loan details and pricing for accuracy. Prepare daily or periodic reports on lock activity, expiring locks, pending requests, and pricing issues. Follow internal controls, audit requirements, and documentation standards. Required Qualifications A Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field is preferred. At least 1 year of experience in U.S. mortgage operations, Secondary Marketing, or mortgage rate lock desk operations is preferred. Knowledge of mortgage pricing, rate locks, extensions, relocks, cancellations, and Conventional, FHA, VA, USDA, and applicable Non-QM products is required, along with Excel, Microsoft Office, and pricing analysis skills. Strong analytical, numerical, problem-solving, and communication skills, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple requests under tight deadlines are essential. Key Competencies & Performance Metrics Strong analytical, numerical, and problem-solving skills. Accuracy in mortgage pricing, rate locks, extensions, and relocks. Good time management, prioritization, and attention to detail. Effective communication, teamwork, and knowledge of investor guidelines and compliance requirements. Timely processing of lock requests, quick resolution of pricing issues, and adherence to company policies and service-level agreements (SLAs). Accurate documentation, audit readiness, and reduction of processing errors. Work Schedule & Location Must be available to work according to U.S. mortgage business hours, including the applicable U.S. time zone and market-related deadlines.
